precepts.text: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous. When we meditate on the scriptures day and night and do them, the Lord makes our way prosperous and gives the increase we desire, spiritually and emotionally, when we put our mind on the Lord.
precepts.point: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen. For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption: you will be judged by it. But he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting: when you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord gives blessings, favor, mercy, and abundance.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.” When you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord is going to give you blessings: he will show you favor, have mercy on you, and give you abundance. That is Joshua 1:8: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.”

We should meditate on the scriptures day and night, “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” Meditating and doing is the sowing.

When we do that, the Lord makes our way prosperous. He gives us the abundance we desire, spiritually, emotionally, all the increases we desire, when we put our mind on the Lord. That is reaping of the Spirit.

precepts.text: Camps like that have made themselves students and underlings to foolish men.
precepts.point: Some elders from other camps say that Moses left the truth. It says right there in verse 17, only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses. Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
When Moses died, the mantle passed to Joshua, and the people answered him: “According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee: only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” They hearkened to Moses because they believed he was the man of the Lord. Moses led the people with integrity and character, even while judging Israel in the wilderness, and he kept that integrity all the way.

Yet there are negroes online, some elders from other camps, certain unsavory Black Hebrew Israelite camps, saying that Moses left the truth, that he was off and didn't have the spirit. What are you talking about? It says right there in verse 17: “only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” The Lord was with Moses. Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you.

Because Sirach says, “Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man; neither accept the person of the mighty.” Camps like that have made themselves students and underlings to a negro that's just as dumb as they are.

Israel followed Joshua because they had seen Moses' character in him while he ministered under Moses. The company you keep matters. Joshua was under Moses, and Caleb did the same thing, and they learned integrity and good character by being under a man the Lord was with. Put yourself under a foolish man, and you learn his folly instead.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
What actually brings us peace? Not enlisting in this war, and not hoping America goes back to the old ways. “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee”. The mind that is stayed on the Lord is the mindset of Joshua 1:8: the book of the law does not depart out of your mouth, and you meditate on it day and night.

That is your four chapters a day. That is you not separating yourself, and having that godly conversation consistently, as in Malachi, where they thought upon the Lord's name and a book of remembrance was written. That is making sure the sick among us in the congregations are well taken care of. That is you men doing the blitz, traveling, doing your due diligence by all manner to get out of that black shirt and get out here and teach your people, to become men of valor and soldiers of the Lord, and put in your brick.

You establish yourself on the laws of God. That is your meditation, your chief joy. You're not worried about what is played on the radio, and you could give a damn about what's on the internet unless it is funneled through the Bible so you can keep up with the times.

Then the news, the destruction and the chaos won't worry you. You'll have a Coke bottle smile from one ear to the next, because you know the mysteries. You're not fearful of freedom. The mind that meditates on the law day and night is the mind the Lord keeps in perfect peace.

precepts.point: If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth. Try talking with your tongue stuck to the roof of your mouth: that is how Christians sound to those who know the Bible, making up doctrines from seminary schools and sounding fine only to other Christians. And you cannot prefer Jerusalem above your chief joy if you do not know you are Israel.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
What is supposed to be in your mouth? “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.” The book of the law, the Bible, God's laws: that is what belongs in your mouth, the word of God and the laws of God.

But because we have been so wicked, God made our tongue to cleave to the roof of our mouth, and we sound like idiots trying to break this Bible down. When you are a Christian you do not know it, so you say strange things and strange doctrines, like the burning mountain is a meteorite. That is the stupidness that comes out when the law is not in the mouth.

Look at the black pastor today, preaching a sermon while getting a haircut: soft, sweet, moist, squishy, and a leader in the black church. That is the result when the law departs out of the mouth of those who are supposed to teach it.

So Psalms 137:6 is the curse on the tongue for forgetting Jerusalem, and Joshua 1:8 is what the tongue was made for: the law, spoken and meditated on day and night, so that we may observe to do all that is written therein.

precepts.text: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; meditate therein day and night.
precepts.point: Whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty and continueth therein, a doer of the work, shall be blessed in his deed. Christ's grace is the platform to build on, so there is no going backwards.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
James says the blessed man is the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, “not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work”. Joshua says the same thing another way: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”.

Ask yourself, brothers and sisters: are you meditating in this book they call the Bible? Don't lie to yourself. If you have to ask, it means you need to do it more, because it is supposed to be a natural thing.

Why meditate on it day and night? Because we want to keep the ministry blameless, and because we know the job of Satan: he is like a roaring lion, waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments. When you meditate on something day and night, you have no time for foolishness. It is like the scriptures warning not to be idle, because when you are idle you fall back into sin. When you are constantly in the scriptures, your mind is focused on keeping the commandments. That is the pattern: stay focused.

The enemy is at work every day. Turn off the TV and the phone and you might have a two or three percent upper hand, but as long as these devices and human beings exist on this earth, our battle is serious and we are battling every day.

Joshua goes on: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. That is James 1:25 again. The perfect law of liberty is what we look into: the commandments, the mercy of God, the grace of God. Christ died on the cross and gave us that grace as the platform to build upon, so we can no longer go backwards; now we have to go forward. The one who is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work “shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his teaching and his business, whatever he does.

precepts.why:
“And all the people saw the cloudy pillar stand at the tabernacle door: and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man in his tent door. And the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.” All the people worshipped at their tent doors while the Lord spake unto Moses face to face.

“And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle.” Joshua, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle; he wanted to be right there with his leader. That is why he is Moses' minister: he cleaved to Moses, and learned the ins and outs of how his leader was successful. It is not being around the longest that qualifies a man to rise up in another's stead; it is being the diligent servant.

That is the spirit the young men coming up in this truth should aspire to: cleave to your leadership.

precepts.text: Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation to lead them out and bring them in, that Israel be not as sheep without a shepherd.
precepts.point: Why was Joshua the one anointed? When the Lord told Moses he would see the land but not enter it, Moses did not argue or justify himself. His humble response was to ask the Lord to set a man over the congregation, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd. Moses brought no candidates; he let the Lord pick, and the Lord picked the young man who had cleaved to him: promotion comes from the Lord, and he selects the leaders over his people.

Why was Joshua the one anointed? When the Lord told Moses he would see the land but not enter it, Moses did not argue or justify himself. His humble response was this: “Let the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation, Which may go out before them, and which may go in before them, and which may lead them out, and which may bring them in; that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd.”

Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation to lead them out and bring them in, that Israel be not as sheep without a shepherd. He brought no candidates; he let the Lord pick.

And he said set a man over the congregation, not a woman, because women were never ordained to lead the children of Israel; that does not fit the divine order of the Most High.

That is how “Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise” comes to Joshua and no one else.

precepts.text: Days as the days of heaven upon the earth; if ye diligently keep the commandments, every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours, no man shall be able to stand before you, and the Lord shall lay the fear and dread of you upon all the land, the very promise repeated to Joshua.
precepts.point: This is the same word the Lord foretold to Moses that Joshua now fulfills. The promised land was meant to be as the days of heaven upon the earth, and the condition was diligently keeping all the commandments, to love the Lord, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; then the Lord would drive out nations greater and mightier than Israel. Heaven was never about everybody being equal and holding hands; heaven is Israel gaining possession and power over the nations, and that has always been the gospel.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
This is the same word the Lord foretold to Moses that Joshua now fulfills. Moses told Israel the promised land was meant to be “as the days of heaven upon the earth.” The condition was “if ye shall diligently keep all these commandments which I command you, to do them, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; Then will the Lord drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves.”

Then the very promise repeated to Joshua: “Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be. There shall no man be able to stand before you: for the Lord your God shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that ye shall tread upon, as he hath said unto you.”

Heaven was never about everybody being equal and holding hands; heaven is Israel gaining possession and power over the nations, and that has always been the gospel. The proof that we have not kept the commandments is that we own nothing today. Even land bought and paid for is not truly yours: fail to pay the real estate tax and it is taken by eminent domain and sold at auction. It was never meant to be that way; Israel was supposed to have ownership of the earth.

That is what the Lord was telling Joshua: every place the sole of your foot treads, from the wilderness and Lebanon unto the great river Euphrates and unto the great sea, is given to the children of Israel. Heaven is Israel gaining possession and power over the nations; it has always been the gospel. Under Christ the difference is an eternal reign, with our spirit changed so we cannot transgress. The word did not profit them because it was not mixed with faith; let it profit us.

precepts.text: Wisdom teaches fortitude, the very strength and courage the Lord commanded Joshua to have.
precepts.point: It takes strength to observe to do according to all the law; that is why the scriptures speak of building up your faith and being exercised in the things you learn. You have to be spiritually fit to survive in this truth, especially as a leader. The word for being strong and very courageous is fortitude, one of the virtues that comes with wisdom.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
The first thing the Lord commands the new leader is to be strong and of a good courage, and he has to reiterate it: “Only be thou strong and very courageous”. The word for being strong and very courageous is fortitude, and Solomon names it among the virtues that come with wisdom: “And if a man love righteousness her labours are virtues: for she teacheth temperance and prudence, justice and fortitude: which are such things, as men can have nothing more profitable in their life.”

Wisdom teaches fortitude, the very strength and courage the Lord commanded Joshua to have. This truth is not for the weak, not for people easily discouraged when trials and tribulations occur and people bring burdens of matters unto you; you have to be built for it. You are dealing with the Israelites, a stiffnecked, rebellious, cold hearted people, so there is no room for mild moments or weak moments.

It takes strength to “observe to do according to all the law”; that is why the scriptures speak of building up your faith and being exercised in the things you learn. You have to be spiritually fit to survive in this truth, especially as a leader.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

All thy communication in the law of the most High: that is “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth”. Keep company where the law is the talk, and the law stays in your mouth.

precepts.text: The chapter speaks of wisdom as a she who orders all things sweetly and mightily.
precepts.point: Solomon shows what a companion meditation makes of wisdom: when he came into his house he reposed himself with her, for her conversation has no bitterness and living with her has no sorrow, but mirth and joy. note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“Wisdom reacheth from one end to another mightily: and sweetly doth she order all things.” The chapter speaks of wisdom as a she, who orders all things sweetly and mightily.

Solomon goes on in this chapter to show what a companion meditation makes of that wisdom, when a man comes into his house and reposes himself with her. Wisdom that reaches from one end to another mightily is what meditating in the law day and night gives you.

precepts.text: Solomon pondered these things in his heart; that pondering is the meditation the Lord commanded Joshua.

Solomon pondered these things in his heart; that pondering is the meditation the Lord commanded Joshua. When you ponder the whole benefit package that comes with wisdom, you understand that to be allied unto wisdom is immortality; the wiser you get, the more spiritually invincible you become.

precepts.text: Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide; he had an appointed place and time of day, alone at the going down of the sun, to reflect on the works of the Most High.
precepts.point: Make meditation a daily custom, a holy habit, as our forefathers did: somewhere alone and peaceful where the mind can be clear, because you cannot meditate in the middle of activity and noise. note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels were coming.” Isaac had an appointed place and time of day, alone at the going down of the sun, to reflect on the works of the Most High.

Make meditation a daily custom, a holy habit, as our forefathers did: somewhere alone and peaceful where the mind can be clear, because you cannot meditate in the middle of activity and noise. Isaac went out to the field at the eventide; that is the pattern for meditating in the law day and night.

precepts.text: Meditate continually, as a habit, and he shall establish thine heart and give thee wisdom at thine own desire.
precepts.point: Make meditation a daily custom, a holy habit, as our forefathers did: somewhere alone and peaceful where the mind can be clear, because you cannot meditate in the middle of activity and noise. When you meditate continually on the commandments, the Lord establishes your heart, and the evil thoughts you battle begin to flush out of your mind.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:

And there is the promise with it: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine own desire. When you meditate continually on the commandments, the Lord establishes your heart, and the evil thoughts you battle begin to flush out of your mind.

precepts.text: The mind has to stay on these things, and it will not stay there without continual meditation.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.” The mind has to stay on these things, and it will not stay there without continual meditation.

That is why the Lord said day and night. A mind stayed on the Most High is kept in perfect peace, and the mind only stays there through the daily custom of meditating in the law, with the evil thoughts flushed out.

precepts.text: Every king of Israel had to write himself a copy of the law and read therein all the days of his life, not just on a sabbath, that he may learn to fear the Lord and keep the words of this law to do them; you are what you eat, and what you put within comes out in your conversation and your actions.
precepts.point: That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: the end goal of talking about the commandments and meditating on the commandments is to do the commandments. Attending every class, hearing every breakdown, and keeping every precept list is all in vain if you never do thus saith the Lord; not doing the word of God is why we went into slavery and sit at the bottom of society.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
Every king of Israel had the same charge Joshua got: “when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites: And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life: that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them”.

He had to write himself a copy of the law and read therein all the days of his life, not just on a sabbath, that he may learn to fear the Lord and keep the words of this law to do them. You are what you eat, and what you put within comes out in your conversation and your actions. That is the law in the mouth, the meditation day and night, and the observing to do, all in one charge to the king.

Ezekiel shows the people who never get there: “And they come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people, and they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their covetousness.”

“And, lo, thou art unto them as a very lovely song of one that hath a pleasant voice, and can play well on an instrument: for they hear thy words, but they do them not.” Many hear the word as a lovely song, loving to hear the scriptures broken down, but they hear the words and do them not. Hearing so much does not earn you credit for doing. Attending every class, hearing every breakdown, and keeping every precept list is all in vain if you never do thus saith the Lord.

precepts.text: Then shalt thou prosper, if thou takest heed to fulfil the statutes and judgments which the Lord charged Moses with concerning Israel; the same charge, be strong and of good courage.
precepts.point: For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. Thus saith God, the second you transgress the commandments of the Lord you cannot prosper, so any pastor teaching prosperity while saying the law is done away with is teaching a lie. note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
David gave Solomon the same charge the Lord gave Joshua: “Then shalt thou prosper, if thou takest heed to fulfil the statutes and judgments which the Lord charged Moses with concerning Israel: be strong, and of good courage; dread not, nor be dismayed.”

Then shalt thou prosper, if thou takest heed to fulfil the statutes and judgments; and with it, be strong and of good courage. That is Joshua 1:8: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. The formula for success was handed down from Joshua to the kings of Israel.

precepts.text: Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly but meditates in the law day and night; he brings forth fruit, meaning action, his spirit does not wither, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

“Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.” The blessed man walks not in the counsel of the ungodly but meditates in the law day and night, the very words the Lord spoke to Joshua.

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.” He brings forth fruit, meaning action; his spirit does not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. That is “then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success”: the true prosperity doctrine.

precepts.text: As a nation of people, if they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity.

precepts.why:
“If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.” As a nation of people, if they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity.

Real prosperity never came from sowing a seed into a basket; it comes from obeying the laws of the Most High, and that applies to us as a whole nation of people. Obey and serve him, and the days are spent in prosperity and the years in pleasures.

Prosperity follows the mouth, the meditation, and the doing; it belongs to the people that love Jerusalem by keeping the commandments of her God.

“And the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith God, Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper? because ye have forsaken the Lord, he hath also forsaken you.”

precepts.point: Have not I commanded thee: not being afraid is a commandment. Fear does not come from the Most High; the only fear he deals with is fearing him and the judgments you suffer for disobeying him. Being scared of what man can do to you is a spirit from the devil, not from God.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed”. Not being afraid is a commandment. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.”

Fear does not come from the Most High; the only fear he deals with is fearing him and the judgments you suffer for disobeying him. Being scared of what man can do to you is a spirit from the devil, not from God. If the spirit of fear comes upon you, it is not of God. The Lord gave us the spirit of power; as long as you serve and obey him, there is nothing to be scared of.

precepts.text: Nehemiah discerned the man urging him to hide in the temple was hired that he should be afraid, and do so, and sin; a leader who becomes afraid of what the heathen threaten is in the midst of sin, so if you carry a fearful spirit, repent.
precepts.point: Have not I commanded thee: not being afraid is a commandment. Fear does not come from the Most High; the only fear he deals with is fearing him and the judgments you suffer for disobeying him. Being scared of what man can do to you is a spirit from the devil, not from God.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
Nehemiah discerned the man urging him to hide in the temple: “Therefore was he hired, that I should be afraid, and do so, and sin, and that they might have matter for an evil report, that they might reproach me.”

He was hired that Nehemiah should be afraid, and do so, and sin. A leader who becomes afraid of what the heathen threaten is in the midst of sin. That is why the Lord commanded Joshua, “be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed”: fear leads a leader into sin and gives the enemy matter for an evil report. So if you carry a fearful spirit, repent.

precepts.text: The fearful head the list of those who take the dive into the lake of fire, before the unbelieving, the abominable, and the murderers.
precepts.point: Look at the end result of a fearful spirit that is never shaken: the fearful are the first named of those whose part is in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone. The Lord gave us the spirit of power; as long as you serve and obey him, there is nothing to be scared of.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
Look at the end result of a fearful spirit that is never shaken: “But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.”

The fearful head the list of those who take the dive into the lake of fire, before the unbelieving, the abominable, and the murderers. That is how serious the commandment “be not afraid” is. The fearful are the first named.

precepts.text: Be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might; that is the spirit given in place of fear.
precepts.point: Look at the end result of a fearful spirit that is never shaken: the fearful are the first named of those whose part is in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone. The Lord gave us the spirit of power; as long as you serve and obey him, there is nothing to be scared of.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.” That is the spirit given in place of fear: the Lord gave us the spirit of power, and the strength is in the Lord and in the power of his might, not in ourselves.

“Be strong and of a good courage”, the Lord told Joshua, “for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.” As long as you serve and obey him, there is nothing to be scared of.

precepts.text: The deal Moses made: go armed before the Lord to war until the land be subdued, and afterward ye shall return and be guiltless, and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.
precepts.point: The word to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh goes back to Numbers 32. They had very much cattle, and when they saw the land on this side Jordan was a good place for it, they asked to dwell there. Moses charged them: before you settle, your armed men pass over before your brethren, all the mighty men of valour, and help them fight; when your brethren have rest and possession, then return to the land of your possession toward the sunrising and enjoy it.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
The word to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh goes back to Numbers 32. They had very much cattle, and when they saw the land on this side Jordan was a good place for it, they asked to dwell there. This was the deal Moses made: “If ye will do this thing, if ye will go armed before the Lord to war, And will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord, until he hath driven out his enemies from before him, And the land be subdued before the Lord: then afterward ye shall return, and be guiltless before the Lord, and before Israel; and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.”

Before you settle, your armed men pass over before your brethren, all the mighty men of valour, and help them fight until the land be subdued; then afterward ye shall return and be guiltless, and this land shall be your possession. That is why Joshua tells them, “Remember the word which Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you”: their wives, little ones and cattle remain, but they pass before their brethren armed until their brethren have rest and possession, and then return to their own land toward the sunrising and enjoy it.

precepts.text: The king's servants said, Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint; always ready, whatever is needed.
precepts.point: The boundary stands: if an order breaks the commandments of God, no. But if it falls within the boundaries of the commandments, be willing without hesitation to do what your leader tells you. Whatever position you hold in the body, you are a servant, and when the opportunity comes to fulfill an order you need to be ready; that readiness is the spirit we lack in Israel.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“All that thou commandest us we will do, and whithersoever thou sendest us, we will go.” That is loyalty and the willingness to obey orders, something the Lord loves, and part of the spirit it takes to obtain the promised land. The king's servants had the same spirit: “Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint.”

Always ready, whatever is needed. The boundary stands: if an order breaks the commandments of God, no. But if it falls within the boundaries of the commandments, be willing without hesitation to do what your leader tells you. Whatever position you hold in the body, you are a servant, and when the opportunity comes to fulfill an order you need to be ready. That readiness is the spirit we lack in Israel.

precepts.text: When Judas fell and Simon rose up in his stead, the people vowed the same obedience to the new leader, just as Israel did with Joshua after Moses.
precepts.point: The boundary stands: if an order breaks the commandments of God, no. But if it falls within the boundaries of the commandments, be willing without hesitation to do what your leader tells you. Whatever position you hold in the body, you are a servant, and when the opportunity comes to fulfill an order you need to be ready; that readiness is the spirit we lack in Israel.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee”. When Judas fell and Simon rose up in his stead, the people vowed the same obedience to the new leader: “Thou shalt be our leader instead of Judas and Jonathan thy brother. Fight thou our battles, and whatsoever, thou commandest us, that will we do.”

Just as Israel did with Joshua after Moses. When a leader falls and a new leader rises in his stead, that is who the Lord appointed over you, and he is owed the same respect the original leader had. Moses himself asked the Lord to select the man; the selection is spiritual.

“Whosoever he be that doth rebel against thy commandment, and will not hearken unto thy words in all that thou commandest him, he shall be put to death”: that is how our forefathers rolled. Under Christ there is grace and mercy, but the order still works by delegation; instruction passes from Christ through the brothers he sets over you, and refusing the brother who carries the order is refusing the one who sent it. Rehearse these righteous acts of taking orders while you have grace.

precepts.text: When a man keeps and meditates on the law and does it, he makes his way prosperous and has good success, which is why the willing work on the temple succeeded.
precepts.point: The workmen perfected the work and set the house of God in its state, then brought the rest of the money to make vessels of gold and silver to minister and offer with, and they offered burnt offerings continually all the days of Jehoiada.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

precepts.why:
“This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” When a man keeps the law, meditates on it and does it, he makes his way prosperous and has good success.

That is why the willing work on the temple succeeded. They brought in “the collection that Moses the servant of God laid upon Israel in the wilderness”, doing what was written, and “all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and brought in, and cast into the chest, until they had made an end.” They “gathered money in abundance”, and “the work was perfected by them, and they set the house of God in his state, and strengthened it.”

Money was a defense here, because it paid the skilled brothers who got the temple work done. Not everyone had the same task: masons, carpenters, and such as “wrought iron and brass” each had their charge, and every man had to listen to a manager, for business requires order and submission to authority. So we must deal righteously with our people today, treating a brother’s business as a place to help the family and the body. The good success came even to the rest of the money, “whereof were made vessels for the house of the Lord”, and “they offered burnt offerings in the house of the Lord continually all the days of Jehoiada.”

precepts.text: Josiah declining neither to the right nor left is the charge to Joshua: observe to do according to all the law, turn not from it, and meditate in it day and night that thy way may be prosperous.
precepts.point: In the eighth year of his reign, while yet young, he begins to seek after the God of David, and in the twelfth year he begins to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, groves, and images.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
The charge to Joshua: “Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper whithersoever thou goest.” And “thou shalt meditate therein day and night”, “for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.”

Josiah is that charge kept. He “walked in the ways of David his father, and declined neither to the right hand, nor to the left.” He observed to do according to the law, turned not from it, and so he reigned “in Jerusalem one and thirty years.”

precepts.text: Meditate in the law day and night and observe to do it, and then your way shall be prosperous and you shall have good success, which is the same promise given to the blessed man.
precepts.point: The Most High knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the ungodly shall perish. This is a reminder as we walk through these last days not to roll with ungodly people or anyone who is halfway in and halfway out, because the Most High deals only with those walking righteously. You cannot excuse a work Christmas party as just appeasing people, because the righteous do everything they can to walk in the way of the godly and make no excuses.

note.label: Psalm 1: Blessed Is the Man That Walketh Not in the Counsel of the Ungodly

precepts.why:

Meditate in the law day and night and observe to do it, and then your way shall be prosperous and you shall have good success. That is the blessed man's prosperity: it comes from meditating in the commandments day and night and doing them.

You will be successful and prosper if you actually meditate in the commandments day and night and do them, not merely think about scriptures the way many of us did in Christianity. The ungodly are not so; they will not prosper like the righteous, but are like the chaff which the wind drives away.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: Now let us say you lack confidence, or you need more confidence. Here are some practical things. And when I say practical, that means you must put these things into practice. You must do them, to help develop and boost your confidence. Confidence is not something that you have naturally. It is something that has to be developed over a pattern of good works. Over a period of time you will start to develop a thought process that exudes confidence.

Number one: read your Bible every day. I am going to say that again. I cannot stress that enough. If you want confidence, the number one thing you must do is read your Bible every day. If Jesus Christ was the word of God that became flesh, and that flesh walked with confidence, and we want that same confidence, but he is not here any more, how do we tap into that spirit? We must tap into the word of God.

This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth. So it shall not depart out of your mouth. If anything is in your mouth, it has to be in your mind first. The only way the word of God is in your mouth is if it is in your mind. Meaning you are reading it, you are studying it, and then your conversation will reflect the word of God.
But thou shalt meditate therein day and night. Often, frequently, regularly.
That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein. Daily.

For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success. So after you meditate in the word, converse about the word, the Bible says then you will make your way prosperous and have good success. The people that we associate with prosperity and success, they all have something in common. And you know what that is? Confidence. The word of God will bring you confidence.

Now there is a key point that we just heard right here in Joshua 1:8, and it did not use this word, but I am going to outline the word for you. Discipline. Reading your Bible every day is a discipline. Discipline builds confidence. Why? Because discipline is a consistent pattern of success. If you want to build confidence, you have to put yourself continually in a position of being successful. So when you say you are going to read your Bible every day and you do it, that means you were successful every day. I said I am going to read four chapters today. I did it. I was successful. I said I was going to read four chapters tomorrow. I was successful. Continuing to do that day in and day out develops a conditioning in your mind of being successful.

You want to add these disciplines to your life, starting with the word of God. Even something as small as what time you wake up. If you say you are going to wake up at eight, it is best to wake up at eight. What was that? That was success. But you keep hitting the snooze to eight ten and eight twenty and eight thirty. You know what happens every time you hit the snooze? You produce failure, and you accept failure. So what would be better is for you just to set your alarm at eight thirty and get up at eight thirty, than to set your alarm at eight and keep hitting the snooze. Because every time you hit the snooze, you are conditioning yourself subconsciously to fail. I failed to get up at eight. I failed to get up at eight ten. I failed to get up at eight twenty. And now I am up at eight thirty. Get rid of the failure out of your life. Do what you say you are going to do. That is going to build your confidence over a period of time.

points: Joshua is called Moses' minister because when Moses was the leader, Joshua was the one always cleaving to him. He was not close to Moses in age; he was one of the young men that cleaved unto his elder, and if Moses was a good leader, beloved among the children of Israel, who better to rise up in his stead than the man who has his spirit?

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: That is the spirit the young men coming up in this truth should aspire to: cleave to your leadership. It is not being around the longest that qualifies a man to rise up in another's stead; it is being the diligent servant who learned the ins and outs of how his leader was successful, and even observed his leader's mistakes so he knows what not to do in that position.

Why was Joshua the one anointed? When the Lord told Moses he would see the land but not enter it, Moses did not argue or justify himself. His humble response was to ask the Lord to set a man over the congregation, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd. Moses brought no candidates; he let the Lord pick, and the Lord picked the young man who had cleaved to him: promotion comes from the Lord, and he selects the leaders over his people.

Moses said set a man over the congregation, not a woman, because women were never ordained to lead the children of Israel; that does not fit the divine order of the Most High. Miriam was a prophetess and one of the chief women, and she led the women; women have a real role in the nation, but leading the body is not it. When Miriam got puffed up and spoke against Moses, she was judged.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you: the Lord let Joshua know that everywhere his foot stepped on this path would belong to the children of Israel, from the wilderness and Lebanon unto the great river Euphrates and unto the great sea toward the going down of the sun. These are the borders of the journey he would lead them through.

The proof that we have not kept the commandments is that we own nothing today. Even land bought and paid for is not truly yours: fail to pay the real estate tax and it is taken by eminent domain and sold at auction. It was never meant to be that way; Israel was supposed to have ownership of the earth.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: As I was with Moses, so I will be with thee: not any man would be able to stand before Joshua all the days of his life. When the Lord tells you that, you carry the spirit that backs down from nothing.

This is the same word the Lord foretold to Moses that Joshua now fulfills. The promised land was meant to be as the days of heaven upon the earth, and the condition was diligently keeping all the commandments, to love the Lord, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; then the Lord would drive out nations greater and mightier than Israel. Heaven was never about everybody being equal and holding hands; heaven is Israel gaining possession and power over the nations, and that has always been the gospel.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

He has to reiterate it: only be thou strong. You are dealing with the Israelites, a stiffnecked, rebellious, cold hearted people, so there is no room for mild moments or weak moments.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: It takes strength to observe to do according to all the law; that is why the scriptures speak of building up your faith and being exercised in the things you learn. You have to be spiritually fit to survive in this truth, especially as a leader. The word for being strong and very courageous is fortitude, one of the virtues that comes with wisdom.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: This verse is the recipe for success, the formula for success, the true prosperity doctrine, and it has three steps: the law in your mouth, meditation day and night, and observing to do all that is written therein.

This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth: when you open your mouth, what comes out is supposed to be scriptural; your conversation has to be modeled after what this book says. When people leave this truth the Lord removes his words out of their mouth, and their whole conversation changes: nothing is left but slander, falsehood, strange doctrines, and flattering speech.

Thou shalt meditate therein day and night: to meditate is to think deeply and carefully, to contemplate, consider, ponder, and muse. Many read their four chapters a day, listen to videos, and quote their precept lists, but never meditate on what they read. You cannot just slap the butter on the biscuit; you have to let it sink into every layer.

Solomon shows what a companion meditation makes of wisdom: when he came into his house he reposed himself with her, for her conversation has no bitterness and living with her has no sorrow, but mirth and joy. Get in the habit of chilling with wisdom when you get home. When you ponder the whole benefit package that comes with wisdom, you understand that to be allied unto wisdom is immortality; the wiser you get, the more spiritually invincible you become.

Make meditation a daily custom, a holy habit, as our forefathers did: somewhere alone and peaceful where the mind can be clear, because you cannot meditate in the middle of activity and noise. When you meditate continually on the commandments, the Lord establishes your heart, and the evil thoughts you battle begin to flush out of your mind.

That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: the end goal of talking about the commandments and meditating on the commandments is to do the commandments. Attending every class, hearing every breakdown, and keeping every precept list is all in vain if you never do thus saith the Lord; not doing the word of God is why we went into slavery and sit at the bottom of society.

For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. Thus saith God, the second you transgress the commandments of the Lord you cannot prosper, so any pastor teaching prosperity while saying the law is done away with is teaching a lie. Real prosperity never came from sowing a seed into a basket; it comes from obeying the laws of the Most High, and that applies to us as a whole nation of people.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: Have not I commanded thee: not being afraid is a commandment. Fear does not come from the Most High; the only fear he deals with is fearing him and the judgments you suffer for disobeying him. Being scared of what man can do to you is a spirit from the devil, not from God.

Look at the end result of a fearful spirit that is never shaken: the fearful are the first named of those whose part is in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone. The Lord gave us the spirit of power; as long as you serve and obey him, there is nothing to be scared of.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: The word to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh goes back to Numbers 32. They had very much cattle, and when they saw the land on this side Jordan was a good place for it, they asked to dwell there. Moses charged them: before you settle, your armed men pass over before your brethren, all the mighty men of valour, and help them fight; when your brethren have rest and possession, then return to the land of your possession toward the sunrising and enjoy it.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: All that thou commandest us we will do, and whithersoever thou sendest us we will go: that is loyalty and the willingness to obey orders, something the Lord loves, and part of the spirit it takes to obtain the promised land.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so we will hearken unto thee: when a leader falls and a new leader rises in his stead, that is who the Lord appointed over you, and he is owed the same respect the original leader had. Moses himself asked the Lord to select the man; the selection is spiritual.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: Whosoever rebels against thy commandment and will not hearken unto thy words shall be put to death: that is how our forefathers rolled. Under Christ there is grace and mercy, but the order still works by delegation; instruction passes from Christ through the brothers he sets over you, and refusing the brother who carries the order is refusing the one who sent it. Rehearse these righteous acts of taking orders while you have grace.
